Charter refutation, round 1, fresh critic. Stop 1 is 5780346246; this attacks its refutation-target. Read at 7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd via git show.

## Re-verification of the four named tests at dispatch-sha

All four pin-reads land at the cited lines.

- `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.test.ts:158` fences a blocked basename that contains a newline (#4840); `:162` builds the basename from "evil" + LF + "inject.xbrief.json".
- `packages/core/src/release/release-input.test.ts:180` symlink xbrief root fails before target reads; `:186` symlinkSync(target, join(root, "xbrief")).
- `packages/core/src/release/release-input.test.ts:229` keeps a POSIX backslash in a committed filename across all three views; `:231` commitArtifact of pending/foo-backslash-bar.xbrief.json.
- `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.test.ts:1964` refuses a symlink that escapes to an external regular file; `:1973` symlinkSync(outsideFile, join(root, pointer)).

## blocks-the-design 1 — the success condition is unreachable inside the target's own scope boundary

The refutation-target ends "so `task check` can exit 0". `verify:orphan-active` is a dep of `check:framework-source` (`Taskfile.yml:461-464`, invoked with CLI_ARGS "--changed-only"). The issue reports that lane red on CI for this same SHA (run 35747255508), and the Gate stamp rules it out of arc on the strength of a local pass that "scanned 0 running briefs".

A `--changed-only` scan with nothing in scope is a vacuous pass. It is not evidence the lane is green on this SHA; it is evidence the lane had nothing to look at. And a lane that sits inside `check:framework-source` cannot be out of an arc whose success condition is that same gate exiting 0. As written the target can be fully satisfied — all four tests finishing on win32, no Linux assertion weakened — and `task check` still exits non-zero.

Pick one: narrow the target to "the `ts:check-lane` test phase completes on win32", or pull orphan-active back in scope. Do not keep a whole-motion success clause bounded by a scope that excludes a lane inside the motion.

## blocks-the-design 2 — instance-scoped target for a class-scoped defect, and the class is already measurable

Measured at the dispatch SHA: 80 test files under `packages/core/src` call `symlinkSync`. 29 of them contain no `skipIf` guard anywhere in the file. Both files in this issue are on that unguarded list — `release/release-input.test.ts` and `scope/acceptance-evidence.test.ts`.

That leaves 27 same-class files whose Windows behaviour this run says nothing about. It says nothing because `check:framework-source` fans roughly 40 deps in parallel and the only lane outcome reported here is `ts:check-lane`. "Four tests failed" is the first-observed red in a parallel fan, not an enumerated blocker set.

Fixing four named instances buys one green release and leaves 27 candidates to surface on the next Windows release, one release at a time. The target should name the class — unguarded `symlinkSync` in test fixtures — and what closes it, not four instances.

## blocks-the-design 3 — "mechanism-shaped: true" does not hold; this is conformance against a mechanism that already landed

The Gate stamp claims mechanism-shaped. The mechanism exists and was changelogged.

`CHANGELOG.md:504` (#4344): "Doctor escaping-symlink test skips on Windows without symlink privilege. containDepositInstallRoot rejects an escaping symlink still asserts on platforms that can create the symlink; EPERM/EACCES on win32 skips instead of failing task check." Implemented at `doctor/branches.test.ts:56-74` as a capability probe wrapped around the `symlinkSync` call, calling `ctx.skip()` on EPERM/EACCES and rethrowing otherwise. The sibling dir/junction fallback is production code at `doctor/openclaw-skills.ts:344-357`.

So the policy question this arc would answer was already answered, and answered better than the target's disjunction: probe the capability, skip only the hosts that genuinely cannot, keep asserting everywhere else. What is missing is enforcement. 47 files reference the `itSymlink` idiom and 29 drifted, with no `verify:*` lane binding the convention — in a repo whose merge gate enforces `verify:biome-config`, `verify:encoding`, and `verify:closing-keywords`.

The design defect is the unenforced portability contract. A refutation arc aimed at the four instances leaves that hole exactly where it is.

## sharpens-framing 1 — "(skip or a Windows-legal fixture)" is a false binary over three different root causes

The parenthetical homogenizes four failures that have three distinct causes and three different correct answers.

- **Test 2 (`release-input.test.ts:186`) is a plain fixture bug, not a platform limit.** The target is a directory and no type argument is passed, so Node defaults to "file" on win32 — which fails for a directory target regardless of Developer Mode. "junction" requires no privilege at all, and this repo already does exactly that at `fs/contained-write.test.ts:460`, `hooks/outside-project-root.test.ts:14`, and `hooks/dispatcher-write-reissue.test.ts:331`. This test should keep asserting on Windows. Skipping it is a strict loss taken for no reason.
- **Test 4 (`acceptance-evidence.test.ts:1973`) is the genuine privilege case.** The target is an external regular file, so a junction cannot substitute. This is where the #4344 capability probe applies — not a blanket skipIf(win32), which also retires the assertion on Windows hosts that do hold the privilege.
- **Test 3 (`release-input.test.ts:229`) has a third option the disjunction excludes.** The byte-preservation claim belongs to `splitGitNulRecordsStrict`, exported from `release/release-input.ts:161`, which already has a direct describe block 116 lines above the failing test in the same file at `release-input.test.ts:113-120`. Feeding it a synthetic NUL-delimited buffer holds the backslash assertion on every platform with no filesystem and no git. Only the git-integration half needs a POSIX-only fixture.
- **Test 1 (`scope.test.ts:162`) is the only irreducible one.** 0x0A falls in the 0-31 range NTFS reserves; that basename cannot exist on win32.

One of four is skip-only. Offering skip as a co-equal option across all four invites the cheapest compliant outcome: three recoverable Windows assertions retired to get a release out.

## sharpens-framing 2 — the no-weakening guard is one-sided

"without weakening the Linux assertions those tests already hold" protects Linux and says nothing about Windows.

Every one of these four guards path-injection or unsafe-node behaviour — newline fencing in an untrusted basename, symlink escape to an external file, backslash-as-separator in a committed path. That is precisely the set of semantics that differ on Windows. Under the guard as written, skipping all four is fully compliant, and the result is a release-input validator whose Windows path handling is unasserted on the one platform that runs Step 5. The failing host and the newly untested platform are the same host.

Make the guard two-sided: no behaviour loses its assertion on any platform where that behaviour is reachable. Reachability, not convenience, decides the skip.

## footnote 1 — citation drift in the pin-read

The issue body and the Gate stamp both attribute test 4 to (#4840). The test title at `acceptance-evidence.test.ts:1964` carries no issue tag; only test 1 at `scope.test.ts:158` does. The line ranges themselves re-verify exactly. Cosmetic, but the stamp is what downstream seats read.

## footnote 2 — the pass count covers one lane

"18436 tests passed, 176 skipped" is `ts:check-lane` alone. Because `check:framework-source` deps run in parallel, that number carries no information about the other roughly 39 lanes on this Windows host. It should not be read as everything else being green here.

## Verdict

The refutation target does not survive as written. The requirement that all four tests finish on win32 is right, but the blanket allowance “skip or a Windows-legal fixture” permits a green Step 5 that drops coverage of a Windows-native escape mechanism.

### blocks-the-design — blanket skip permission can erase the junction safety assertion

Evidence: at `7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd`, an exact targeted Vitest run collected the four named cases and reproduced all four setup failures: newline basename `ENOENT` at `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.test.ts:163`; directory symlink `EPERM` at `packages/core/src/release/release-input.test.ts:186`; POSIX-backslash basename `ENOENT` at `packages/core/src/release/release-input.test.ts:59/231`; and file symlink `EPERM` at `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.test.ts:1973`. The repository already uses both `it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")` for privilege-dependent file symlinks and `process.platform === "win32" ? "junction" : "dir"` for directory-link tests. On this same host, `symlinkSync(target, link, "junction")` succeeded and `lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink()` returned true; `validateReleaseInputs` rejects an `xbrief` root when `lstatSync(...).isSymbolicLink()` is true.

Failure mode: an implementation can satisfy the present wording by skipping all four cases on win32. `task check` then exits cleanly while Windows has no assertion that a junctioned lifecycle root is rejected before target reads. That is not merely lost parity: it removes native coverage at the untrusted-filesystem boundary the test is meant to defend.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind with blanket skip permission. Recut it into a per-fixture contract: use a Windows junction for the `xbrief` directory-link case; allow a win32/capability skip for the external-file symlink case; and allow win32 skips for the newline and literal-POSIX-backslash integration fixtures, whose names cannot be represented with the intended semantics on Windows. Preserve their platform-neutral fencing/record-decoding assertions separately and keep the existing Linux integration assertions unchanged.

The strongest rejected alternative is to apply the repository’s common `itSymlink` win32 skip uniformly. That is appropriate for the file-symlink case and operationally simple, but it is too broad for a directory reparse point that Windows can create without symlink privilege. I would flip this verdict if the target explicitly required the junction assertion and restricted skips to the three non-portable fixtures.

Injection/swarm lens: the newline basename is untrusted display input and the two link cases cross filesystem authority boundaries. No prompt, identity, concurrency, worktree, or shared-state mechanism changes here; the concrete safety obligation is to retain deterministic fencing and containment coverage rather than treating reviewer attention as the control.

The parenthetical does not fit those four results.

A junction keeps the unsafe-node and payloadReads 0 assertions. A win32 skip leaves that check unrun on the host that can execute it.
- Backslash filename. writeFileSync returns ENOENT because Win32 treats the backslash as a separator. Creating the missing parent writes a nested foo/bar.xbrief.json. git update-index --index-info of a stage-0 record prints "Ignoring path xbrief/pending/foo\bar.xbrief.json" and does not index it. The nested file is a different selectedPaths value from the assertion at release-input.test.ts:235. Skip keeps the Linux assertion. The nested fixture replaces it. release-input.ts:207 says not to rewrite a backslash in a git -z path.
- Escaping file symlink. symlinkSync returns EPERM. A junction aimed at the outside file lstats as a symlink, then realpathSync returns ENOENT, so isShippedFilePointer (clauses.ts:671-679) returns false from the catch. That matches a missing path. It does not reach the escape check at clauses.ts:674. A hardlink to an outside file realpath-resolves inside the project. Neither substitute is the escaping file symlink the test names.

Failure mode: the sentence binds one it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32") on all four, the pattern at capacity/backfill.test.ts:7, authz/protected-dest-realpath.test.ts:10, and cache/operations.test.ts:18. Local task check can then exit 0, and the Linux bodies stay. That skip leaves the xbrief-root refusal unrun here, where a junction is the unprivileged reparse point and a read through it succeeds. The same sentence also binds the nested backslash plant, which changes the filename the assertion holds. Those are the authority checks in the tests: which directory the release scanner will read, and which basename is one path component.

Disposition: do not bind that parenthetical. Split the finishes. Use a junction for the xbrief-root test and keep unsafe-node plus payloadReads 0. Skip the newline test and the backslash test on win32, and do not swap in the nested path. For the file symlink, skip only when symlinkSync returns EPERM, and keep the assertion on a host that can create the link.

Road not taken: one skipIf(win32) for all four. It unblocks Step 5, and the Linux run on this SHA already passed the assertions. It loses because the directory junction on this host still trips the lstat predicate and is followed by a read.

Confirming this map binds a split. The xbrief directory-link test uses a junction and keeps asserting. The escaping file-symlink test skips only when the host cannot create the link. The newline basename and the POSIX-backslash git filename skip on win32, because those names cannot exist with the intended meaning. The success bar is those four tests finishing, not the whole of task check.

Forward verdict: the skip-or-fixture parenthetical does not survive; the four setup failures do. Disposition: the bound remedy below. Non-self-arbitration: this parent also wrote the Stop 1 triage; the takes below accept critic headings. This lean does not implement or close the issue.

## What was re-checked

Dispatch SHA 7712f482781c4885fd9d395756e2c316785730dd, this Windows host, Node v24.18.0. The four filesystem operations were re-run. The full vitest lane was not.

- A basename containing a newline fails writeFileSync with ENOENT. scope.test.ts:162 builds that name. Skipping that one test on win32 lets it finish. The Linux file-create assertion stays. The name cannot exist here, so the skip does not drop a reachable assertion.
- symlinkSync of a directory with no type fails with EPERM (release-input.test.ts:186). The same call with type junction succeeds. lstat reports isSymbolicLink true and isDirectory false, and a read through the junction returns the target bytes. validateReleaseInputs reaches release-input.ts:474 and returns the unsafe-node failure with payloadReads 0 before any payload read. The junction bullet keeps both assertions. A win32 skip of this test would drop a check this host can run.
- writeFileSync of a filename containing a POSIX backslash fails with ENOENT (commitArtifact at release-input.ts caller release-input.test.ts:59, test at :231). git update-index --index-info of that path does not index it: ls-files afterwards shows only the other file. Skipping the git-integration test on win32 matches a name Windows will not store. The Linux selectedPaths assertion at :235 stays.
- symlinkSync of an outside regular file fails with EPERM (acceptance-evidence.test.ts:1973). The #4344 probe is the EPERM or EACCES ctx.skip around symlinkSync in doctor/branches.test.ts:60-68. The assertion remains on a host that can create the file symlink.

A junction pointed at that outside file does create. lstat reports a symlink that is neither file nor directory, realpath returns ENOENT, and isShippedFilePointer (clauses.ts:667-679) returns false from the catch, before the escape check at clauses.ts:674. The list's ban on a junction for this case is what stops that test going green on a missing path.

Stop 1 defines P1 as this Windows release Step 5 death: task check exit 201 after the fast preflight because these four fixtures die before the assertion. Run 35747255508 is already out of the arc in that same write-back. The list's success bar is those four finishes, not the rest of task check. That is the same cut. The directory-link refusal still runs on this host.

The newline basename and the two links are untrusted filesystem inputs. The control that stays is deterministic: the junction refusal still runs here, and the file-symlink refusal still runs when symlinkSync succeeds.

## Road not taken

One reading treats the success-bar sentence as voiding the cite, because P1 names task check exit 201 and the list says success is not the whole of task check. That reading loses. Stop 1 already placed run 35747255508 outside this arc and named the four setup deaths as the 201. I would flip if a ts:check-lane run on this SHA showed another setup failure in this same set.

## footnote

The sentence that a backslash may be asserted through splitGitNulRecordsStrict is extra coverage, not another finish required for P1. The unit block at release-input.test.ts:113-121 feeds the records "a" and "b" only. The selectedPaths backslash assertion lives on the Linux git test, which the list keeps. Windows cannot store that committed name, so the win32 skip does not drop a reachable assertion. The bound-remedy list stays as written.

The exclusion that names a verify lane for the #4344 itSymlink convention uses the wrong identifier for work that is already out of this pain. In this tree itSymlink means it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32"), as at capacity/backfill.test.ts:7. The landed #4344 behavior is the EPERM or EACCES probe. The file-symlink bullet already names that probe. The four finishes stay as written.
